conclusion: Black-box amplification in QMA is fundamentally limited, and the recently demonstrated doubly-exponential completeness amplification cannot be improved by generic oracle-relative techniques.

title: Truncation Uncertainties For Accurate Quantum Simulations Of Lattice Gauge Theories
authors: Anthony N. Ciavarella, Siddharth Hariprakash, Jad C. Halimeh, And Christian W. Bauer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2216 (2026).

The encoding of lattice gauge theories onto quantum computers requires a discretization of the gauge field's Hilbert space on each link, which presents errors with respect to the Kogut–Susskind limit. In the electric basis, Hilbert space fragmentation has recently been shown to limit the excitation of large electric fields. Here, we leverage this to develop a formalism for estimating the size of truncation errors in the electric basis. Generically, the truncation error falls off as a factorial of the field truncation. Examples of this formalism are applied to the Schwinger model and a pure U(1) lattice gauge theory. For reasonable choices of parameters, we improve on previous error estimates by a factor of [MATH].

.
tldr: The paper develops a formalism for estimating truncation errors in electric-basis encodings of lattice gauge theories on quantum computers, applied to the Schwinger model and pure U(1) lattice gauge theory.
motivation: Encoding lattice gauge theories onto quantum computers requires truncating the gauge-field Hilbert space per link, introducing errors relative to the Kogut–Susskind limit that must be controlled for accurate simulations.
method: The authors exploit Hilbert-space fragmentation in the electric basis to derive error estimates for truncation, and apply the formalism to the Schwinger model and a pure U(1) lattice gauge theory.
result: They find that truncation errors generically fall off factorially with the field truncation, and for reasonable parameters improve previous error estimates by a factor of [MATH].
conclusion: The proposed truncation-error formalism enables more reliable resource estimates and accuracy assessments for quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories.

title: Measuring A Quantum Measure Exceeding Unity
authors: Sanchari Chakraborti, Rafael D. Sorkin, And Urbasi Sinha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2215 (2026).

The history based formalism known as Quantum Measure Theory (QMT) generalizes the concept of probability-measure so as to incorporate quantum interference. The resulting quantum measure [MATH] is defined for arbitrary events (sets of histories), not just for observables at a fixed moment of time. Thanks to interference effects, [MATH] can exceed unity, exhibiting its non-classical nature in a particularly striking manner. Here, in an optical experiment, we illustrate an ancilla based filtering scheme that gives operational meaning to the quantum measure. For a specific photonic event [MATH], we report a measured value of [MATH], which within errors agrees with the theoretical value of [MATH], while exceeding the maximum value permissible for a classical probability (namely [MATH]) by [MATH] upper or [MATH] lower percentile widths. The directly observed quantity is an ordinary detector probability [MATH] (or, with laser light, an equivalent power ratio); the value [MATH] is inferred via the calibrated relation [MATH] for our filter. If an unconventional theoretical concept is to play a role in meeting the foundational challenges of quantum theory, it seems important to bring it into contact with experiment as much as possible. Our experiment does this for the quantum measure.

.
tldr: An optical experiment gives operational meaning to the Quantum Measure Theory quantity and observes a quantum measure exceeding the classical probability bound of unity.
motivation: Quantum Measure Theory generalizes probability to include quantum interference, allowing event measures to exceed unity; the authors aim to bring this foundational concept into contact with experiment.
method: The experiment uses an ancilla-based filtering scheme in photonics and infers the quantum measure from a calibrated detector probability or equivalent power ratio.
result: The measured quantum measure for a specific photonic event exceeds unity and agrees with the theoretical prediction within experimental errors.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental demonstration of a nonclassical quantum measure, supporting Quantum Measure Theory and its foundational program.

title: Chaotic Scattering In Ultracold Atom-ion Collisions
authors: Meirav Pinkas, Jonathan Wengrowicz, Nitzan Akerman And Roee Ozeri
abstract: We report on signatures of classical chaos in ultracold collisions between a trapped ion and a free atom. Using numerical simulations, we show that the scattering dynamics can be highly sensitive to initial conditions for various mass ratios and trapping frequencies, indicating the onset of chaos. We quantify this chaotic dynamics by calculating its fractal dimension. We show that for a trapped Sr ion and a free Rb atom chaotic dynamic appears under experimentally relevant conditions, and find its characteristic energy scale. The observation of classical chaos in atom-trapped-ion collisions suggests that signatures of quantum chaos might appear, for example, through a Wigner–Dyson distribution of collisional resonances.
tldr: The paper numerically identifies signatures of classical chaos in ultracold collisions between a trapped ion and a free atom, characterized by fractal dimension and a characteristic energy scale.
motivation: Atom-ion collisions are relevant to trapped-ion experiments, and the authors investigate whether the underlying scattering dynamics can become chaotic under experimentally accessible conditions.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of ultracold atom-ion scattering for various mass ratios and trap frequencies, quantify sensitivity to initial conditions, and compute the fractal dimension of the scattering dynamics.
result: They find chaotic dynamics for a trapped Sr ion and free Rb atom under experimentally relevant conditions and estimate the characteristic energy scale; they also suggest possible quantum-chaos signatures such as Wigner-Dyson distributed collisional resonances.
conclusion: Classical chaos can appear in experimentally relevant atom-ion collisions, motivating future searches for quantum chaos signatures in such hybrid cold-atom/trapped-ion systems.

title: Emergence Of Nonclassical Radiation In Strongly Laser-driven Quantum Systems
authors: Christian Hünecke And Stefanie Gräfe Ivan Gonoskov
abstract: We present an analytical framework for the emergence of nonclassical radiation in strongly laser-driven quantum systems, with a focus on high-order harmonic generation (HHG). Starting from a Pauli–Fierz description, we employ a parametric factorization of the coupled light–matter wavefunction that reduces the dynamics to coupled equations for a field-driven electronic state and a quantized light mode. Within this framework, we identify a simple and predictive mechanism for nonclassicality: it originates from the nonlinear dependence of the electronic dipole response on the light-mode coordinate. An approximately constant dipole yields coherent radiation, a linear dependence produces squeezing, and higher-order nonlinearities give rise to Wigner-function negativity. We illustrate this mechanism for atomic and molecular model systems and analyze its scaling in multi-emitter configurations, indicating routes toward high-photon-number nonclassical radiation in HHG. Our results provide a transparent connection between strong-field dynamics and quantum-optical properties of emitted light, offering a basis for engineering nonclassical states in intense laser–matter interactions.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical Pauli-Fierz framework explaining how nonclassical radiation, including squeezing and Wigner negativity, emerges in strongly laser-driven systems such as high-order harmonic generation.
motivation: Strong-field laser-matter interactions produce intense radiation, but the quantum-optical nature of the emitted light and the origin of nonclassicality are not fully transparent.
method: The authors use a parametric factorization of the coupled light-matter wavefunction, reducing the dynamics to a field-driven electronic state coupled to a quantized light mode, and analyze atomic and molecular model systems.
result: Nonclassicality is traced to the nonlinear dependence of the electronic dipole response on the light-mode coordinate: constant dipole gives coherent radiation, linear dependence gives squeezing, and higher-order nonlinearities produce Wigner-function negativity.
conclusion: The framework links strong-field dynamics to quantum-optical properties of emitted light, suggesting routes to engineer high-photon-number nonclassical states in intense laser-matter interactions.

title: Quantized Soliton Transport In Helicoidal Spin–orbit Coupled Bose–Einstein Condensates
authors: Xueping Cheng And Ji Lin Pingping Fang
abstract: Topological pumping provides a robust route to quantized motion under adiabatic modulation, yet its extension to nonlinear matter waves with internal spin degrees of freedom remains an open question. Here we demonstrate quantized soliton transport in a two-component Bose–Einstein condensate with helicoidal spin–orbit coupling, subjected to an adiabatically sliding optical lattice. With each pumping cycle, the helicoidal coupling sustains a periodic inter-component population exchange, while the soliton center-of-mass advances by a quantized displacement set by the Chern number, which is insensitive to both the spin–orbit coupling strength and the Zeeman field. We further identify the Zeeman field as a key control parameter governing both the inter-component dynamics during pumping and the soliton stability after the lattice motion ceases: depending on the Zeeman field strength, the soliton either retains its profile or develops persistent breathing modes. These results demonstrate that the combination of helicoidal spin–orbit coupling and Zeeman field enables topological transport of nonlinear matter waves with independently tunable internal spin dynamics.
tldr: The paper demonstrates quantized topological pumping of solitons in a two-component helicoidal spin–orbit-coupled Bose–Einstein condensate subject to an adiabatically sliding optical lattice, with the displacement per cycle fixed by a Chern number.
motivation: Topological pumping is well established for linear single-particle systems, but its extension to nonlinear matter waves carrying internal spin degrees of freedom, where inter-component dynamics and soliton stability come into play, remains open.
method: A two-component BEC with helicoidal spin–orbit coupling is subjected to an adiabatically moving optical lattice; the soliton dynamics, center-of-mass displacement, and inter-component population exchange are analyzed as functions of the spin–orbit coupling strength and Zeeman field.
result: Each pumping cycle yields a quantized center-of-mass displacement set by the Chern number, independent of spin–orbit coupling strength and Zeeman field, while the Zeeman field controls the periodic inter-component population exchange and whether the soliton retains its shape or develops persistent breathing after pumping stops.
conclusion: Helicoidal spin–orbit coupling combined with a tunable Zeeman field enables topological transport of nonlinear matter waves with independently controllable internal spin dynamics.

title: Sampled-Based Guided Quantum Walk: Non-variational Quantum Algorithm For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Ugo Nzongani, Dylan Laplace Mermoud, Giuseppe Di Molfetta, And Andrea Simonetto
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2234 (2026).

We introduce SamBa-GQW, a novel quantum algorithm for solving binary combinatorial optimization problems of arbitrary degree with no use of any classical optimizer. The algorithm is based on a continuous-time quantum walk on the solution space represented as a graph. The walker explores the solution space to find its way to vertices that minimize the cost function of the optimization problem. The key novelty of our algorithm is an offline classical sampling protocol that gives information about the spectrum of the problem Hamiltonian. Then, the extracted information is used to guide the walker to high quality solutions via a quantum walk with a time-dependent hopping rate. We investigate the performance of SamBa-GQW on several quadratic problems, namely MaxCut, maximum independent set, portfolio optimization, and higher-order polynomial problems such as LABS, MAX-[MATH]-SAT and a quartic reformulation of the travelling salesperson problem. We empirically demonstrate that SamBa-GQW finds high quality approximate solutions on problems up to a size of [MATH] qubits by only sampling poly([MATH]) states among [MATH] possible decisions. Furthermore, SamBa-GQW compares in par with classically optimized variational approaches, such as the variational guided quantum walk and QAOA (the latter when run on deep circuits). This places Samba-GQW as a promising heuristic to tackle combinatorial problems beyond the NISQ regime.

.
tldr: The paper introduces SamBa-GQW, a non-variational continuous-time quantum walk algorithm for binary combinatorial optimization guided by offline classical sampling of the problem Hamiltonian spectrum.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms for combinatorial optimization require classical optimizers and can suffer from trainability and runtime issues, motivating non-variational alternatives that still use problem-specific guidance.
method: SamBa-GQW performs a continuous-time quantum walk on the solution-space graph with a time-dependent hopping rate, using spectral information extracted from polynomial classical sampling to guide the walker toward low-cost solutions.
result: Empirical tests on MaxCut, maximum independent set, portfolio optimization, LABS, MAX-k-SAT, and a quartic TSP formulation show high-quality approximate solutions up to large qubit sizes while sampling only polynomially many states, comparing favorably with variational guided quantum walk and deep-circuit QAOA.
conclusion: The algorithm is presented as a promising heuristic for combinatorial optimization beyond the NISQ regime, although it does not directly address the information-theoretic or thermodynamic research directions of interest.

title: Towards Local And Compositional Measurements In Quantum Field Theory
authors: Robert Oeckl And Adamantia Zampeli
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2232 (2026).

A universal framework for the joint measurement of multiple localized observables in quantum field theory satisfying spacetime locality and compositionality is still lacking. We present an approach to the problem that is based on the one hand on the positive formalism, an axiomatic framework, where it is clear from the outset that we satisfy locality and compositionality, while also having a consistent probabilistic interpretation. On the other hand, the approach is based on standard tools from quantum field theory, in particular the path integral and the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. After an overview of the conceptual foundations we introduce the modulus-square construction as a formalization of the measurement process for the expectation value of an important class of observables including quadratic observables. We show that this construction has many of the desired properties, including positivity, locality, single measurement recovery and compositionality. We introduce a renormalization scheme for the measurement of quadratic observables that also satisfies compositionality, in contrast to previous renormalization schemes. We discuss relativistic causality, confirming that measurements in our scheme are indeed localized in the spacetime regions where the underlying observables have support.

.
tldr: The paper proposes a framework for local and compositional measurements of multiple observables in quantum field theory using the positive formalism, path integrals, and the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism.
motivation: There is no universal framework for jointly measuring multiple localized observables in QFT while preserving spacetime locality and compositionality with a consistent probabilistic interpretation.
method: The authors combine the axiomatic positive formalism with standard QFT tools, introducing a modulus-square construction for measurement expectation values and a renormalization scheme for quadratic observables.
result: The construction satisfies positivity, locality, single-measurement recovery, compositionality, and relativistic causality, with measurements localized in the spacetime support of the underlying observables.
conclusion: The framework provides a promising route toward local and compositional measurements in QFT, including renormalized quadratic observables, though it lies outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Time Symmetry In Quantum Theories And Beyond
authors: John H. Selby, Maria E. Stasinou, Stefano Gogioso, And Bob Coecke
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2221 (2026).

There exists a stark tension among different formulations of quantum theory as some are inherently time-symmetric while others are time-asymmetric. This tension is crisply captured when considering physical theories as theories of processes. We present the process theory of quantum physics, QPhys, which treats classical systems as internal to quantum theory. We provide three ways to incorporate time symmetry in QPhys. The first restricts the process theory of QPhys to one that satisfies an additional retrocausality constraint. The second is a novel approach, which extends the notions of causality and retrocausality to apply to systems along with processes. Utilizing this approach, we create a toy model for particle physics , where the causal and retrocausal systems correspond to particles and anti-particles respectively. The third approach extends QPhys to a supertheory that satisfies neither a causality nor a retrocausality constraint. To avoid unphysical predictions we modify either its composition rule or its processes.

.
tldr: The paper presents a process-theoretic formulation of quantum physics, QPhys, and explores three ways to incorporate time symmetry via causality and retrocausality constraints.
motivation: There is tension between time-symmetric and time-asymmetric formulations of quantum theory, especially when theories are viewed as theories of processes.
method: The authors develop the process theory QPhys, treat classical systems internally, and introduce causality/retrocausality constraints on processes and systems, including a supertheory extension.
result: They obtain a toy particle-physics model where causal and retrocausal systems correspond to particles and antiparticles, and discuss modifications to avoid unphysical predictions.
conclusion: The work offers a categorical/process-theoretic framework for time symmetry in quantum theories, but it is primarily foundational and not directly aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Phason-driven Temperature-dependent Transport In Moiré Graphene
authors: Alex Boschi, Alejandro Ramos-Alonso, Vaidotas Mišeikis, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Fabio Beltram, Stiven Forti, Antonio Rossi, Camilla Coletti, Rafael M Fernandes, Héctor Ochoa And Sergio Pezzini
abstract: The electronic and vibrational properties of 2D materials are dramatically altered by the formation of a moiré superlattice. The lowest-energy phonon modes of the superlattice are two acoustic branches (called phasons) that describe the sliding motion of one layer with respect to the other. Considering their low-energy dispersion and damping, these modes may act as a significant source of scattering for electrons in moiré materials. Here, we investigate temperature-dependent electrical transport in minimally twisted bilayer graphene (TBG), a moiré system developing multiple weakly-dispersive electronic bands and a reconstructed lattice structure. We measure a linear-in-temperature resistivity across the band manyfold above K, preceded by a quadratic temperature dependence. While the linear-in-temperature resistivity is up to two orders of magnitude larger than in monolayer graphene, it is reduced (approximately by a factor of three) with respect to magic-angle TBG. Moreover, it is modulated by the recursive band filling, with minima located close to the full filling of each band. Comparing our results with a semiclassical transport calculation, we show that the experimental trends are compatible with scattering processes mediated by longitudinal phasons, which dominate the resistivity over the contribution from conventional acoustic phonons of the monolayer. Our findings highlight the close relation between vibrational modes unique to moiré materials and carrier transport therein.
tldr: Temperature-dependent transport measurements in minimally twisted bilayer graphene show linear-in-T resistivity attributed to scattering by longitudinal phason modes unique to moiré superlattices.
motivation: The lowest-energy vibrational modes of a moiré superlattice (phasons) are predicted to strongly scatter electrons, but their role in electrical transport had not been experimentally established.
method: The authors measure resistivity versus temperature in minimally twisted bilayer graphene devices across multiple band fillings and compare the data to a semiclassical transport calculation including phason- and acoustic-phonon-mediated scattering.
result: Resistivity is quadratic at low temperature and becomes linear-in-T at higher temperature, up to two orders of magnitude above monolayer graphene but about three times smaller than magic-angle TBG, with minima near full band fillings; the trends agree with longitudinal-phason-dominated scattering.
conclusion: Moiré-specific vibrational modes dominate carrier scattering in twisted bilayer graphene, linking superlattice mechanical structure to electronic transport.

title: Extended Fractional Hofstadter States At High Field In Twisted Bilayer Graphene Above The Magic Angle
authors: Joe Finneyaaron Sharpelinsey K. Rodenbachjian Kangxiaoyu Wangkenji Watanabetakashi Taniguchimarc A. SignificanceElectrons in solids can collectively organize into topological states characterized by integer or fractionally quantized Hall conductance. Fractional states, which rely on strong electron–electron interactions, are typically more fragile than ...
tldr: Transport measurements in twisted bilayer graphene above the magic angle reveal an extended series of fractional Hofstadter states at high magnetic field.
motivation: Fractional Chern and Hofstadter-type states in moiré graphene are interesting because they combine strong correlations with topological band structure, but whether such states survive far above the magic angle was unclear.
method: Magnetotransport measurements on high-quality twisted bilayer graphene devices at large magnetic fields, with Landau fan and Hofstadter diagram analysis interpreted via moiré band modeling.
result: An extended family of fractionally quantized Hall states is observed at high field, forming Hofstadter-like fans that persist above the magic angle.
conclusion: Correlated topological states in twisted bilayer graphene are more robust and richer than expected, extending beyond the magic-angle regime.

title: Finite-temperature Superfluid Depletion Of Disordered Bose Gases
authors: Cord A Müller
abstract: At zero temperature, homogeneous interacting Bose-condensed fluids are entirely superfluid, with remarkable transport properties. A non-superfluid, normal component is induced by finite temperatures and spatial inhomogeneity, the combined effects of which are rather intriguing, and difficult to describe quantitatively. By inhomogeneous Bogoliubov theory, applicable to weakly interacting condensed Bose gases in static external potentials with arbitrary spatial correlations, we calculate the normal fluid density via the transverse current–current correlation. We obtain finite-temperature disorder corrections to the normal fraction known since Laudau’s seminal two-fluid theory, using diagrammatic perturbation theory for systems of any dimensionality, with closed analytical expressions to leading, quadratic order in disorder strength.
tldr: The paper computes finite-temperature disorder corrections to the normal fluid density of weakly interacting Bose gases using inhomogeneous Bogoliubov theory.
motivation: Finite temperature and spatial inhomogeneity jointly induce a normal component in Bose superfluids, but quantitative descriptions of disordered finite-temperature gases are challenging.
method: The authors use inhomogeneous Bogoliubov theory and diagrammatic perturbation theory to calculate the transverse current-current correlation, obtaining analytical expressions to quadratic order in disorder strength for arbitrary dimensionality.
result: Closed analytical expressions are derived for finite-temperature disorder corrections to the normal fluid density, extending Landau's two-fluid theory to disordered weakly interacting Bose gases.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative perturbative framework for superfluid depletion in disordered Bose gases, but it is specialized to ultracold condensed-matter physics and not directly connected to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: From Band Reconstruction To Bogoliubov Dispersion: How Dz 2-band Enhances Iron-based Superconductivity
authors: Jingming Yan, Shendong Su, Guihao Jia, Yucong Peng, Xuanyu Long, Zheng Liu, Pei Ouyang, Qi-Kun Xue And Wei Li
abstract: Conventional understanding of iron-based superconductivity is usually established based on electronic bands at the Fermi level, leaving deeper bands overlooked as potential factor. Here, we expand this view by demonstrating that a deep-lying dz2 band below the Fermi level can be employed to enhance the superconducting paring strength. By using scanning tunneling microscope to mechanically change the crystal lattice of an iron-based superconductor, we observe an upward shift of the deep-lying dz2 band related feature, leading to hybridization with the primary superconducting bands at the Fermi level. We visualize the novel evidence of this band hybridization and resulting enhanced superconducting gap through quasiparticle interference imaging, providing conclusive evidence that engineering such correlations between deep and pairing-active bands is a potent mechanism for amplifying the superconducting gap. This work refines the conventional view of pairing-relevant electronic structures and establishes band hybridization as an effective way to optimize superconducting materials.
tldr: Using STM/STS on an iron-based superconductor, the authors show that mechanically shifting a deep-lying dz2 band upward so it hybridizes with Fermi-level bands enhances the superconducting pairing gap.
motivation: Conventional accounts of iron-based superconductivity focus only on bands at the Fermi level, overlooking whether deeper bands can contribute to pairing strength.
method: The crystal lattice of an iron-based superconductor is mechanically deformed in a scanning tunneling microscope, and quasiparticle interference imaging is used to track the dz2 band feature and the superconducting gap.
result: The deep dz2 band shifts upward and hybridizes with the primary superconducting bands, and this hybridization is correlated with an enhanced superconducting gap.
conclusion: Engineering hybridization between deep and pairing-active bands is proposed as an effective route to amplify superconducting pairing and optimize superconducting materials.

title: From Optical Gain To Lasing With Colloidal Nanocrystals
authors: Ivo Tanghe, Zeger Hens, Dries van Thourhout And Pieter Geiregat
abstract: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are widely explored as optical gain materials, and throughout over 20 years of research their performance is evaluated through transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) using parameters such as gain magnitude, lifetime, and threshold. In this work, we discuss some of the literature values reported and couple that to different gain mechanisms. Next, we take a closer look at how these actually relate to the physical parameters that govern lasing, as described by the semiconductor laser rate equations, and found some discrepancy with what is usually reported and what is necessary. We introduce a new analytical framework that connects TAS data to two new fundamental quantities: the stimulated emission rate, representing the intrinsic light–matter interaction speed, and the carrier recombination time, which determines the competing nonradiative loss channel. Together with the already typically reported transparency density, these parameters enable direct prediction of key laser characteristics, like threshold behavior for both femto- and quasi-CW excitation, without requiring full device fabrication. Applying this methodology to a range of colloidal NC systems, we demonstrate that their intrinsic gain performance approaches that of epitaxially grown quantum wells. Analysis of colloidal NC laser literature data further confirms the consistency and predictive power of this approach. This work establishes a unified basis for interpreting ultrafast spectroscopy of NCs and provides a more quantitative route to benchmarking emerging materials for integrated laser technologies.
tldr: The paper introduces an analytical framework linking transient absorption spectroscopy of colloidal nanocrystals to intrinsic gain parameters (stimulated emission rate, carrier recombination time) that predict lasing thresholds without device fabrication.
motivation: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals are widely studied as optical gain media, but two decades of TAS-based benchmarking using gain magnitude, lifetime, and threshold has been poorly connected to the physical parameters that actually determine lasing.
method: The authors reanalyze literature gain values and gain mechanisms, compare them with semiconductor laser rate equations, and derive a framework converting TAS data into stimulated emission rates and carrier recombination times alongside transparency density.
result: Applying the method across several colloidal nanocrystal systems shows their intrinsic gain performance approaches that of epitaxial quantum wells, and reanalysis of published laser data confirms the approach's consistency and predictive power for femto- and quasi-CW threshold behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a unified, quantitative basis for interpreting ultrafast spectroscopy of nanocrystals and for benchmarking emerging gain materials for integrated laser technologies.

title: Toward High-temperature Superconductivity In Organic Systems
authors: Wenliang Zhu, Hui Ma, Jianfeng Zhang And Mianqi Xue
abstract: Achieving high-temperature superconductivity has long been a formidable challenge. Organic materials, characterized by their flexible intermolecular interactions (including the flexibility of polymer chains) and hydrogen-rich composition, offer significant potential for realizing high-temperature superconductivity under relatively mild conditions. This review comprehensively summarizes the research progress in organic superconducting materials, including organic charge-transfer salts, carbon-based materials, aromatic compounds, and polymers. We elaborate on the structures and superconducting properties of these organic superconductors. Importantly, based on these advances in organic superconductor and ordered conjugated polymers, we propose the implementation of new material platforms and experimental methods to facilitate the discovery of new organic superconducting materials and explore high-temperature superconductivity. This includes constructing or searching for new materials, doping carriers, applying high pressure, and forming heterojunctions.
tldr: This review surveys organic superconducting materials and proposes experimental strategies for discovering high-temperature organic superconductors.
motivation: High-temperature superconductivity remains a major challenge, and organic materials with flexible intermolecular interactions and hydrogen-rich compositions may enable superconductivity under milder conditions.
method: The authors review organic charge-transfer salts, carbon-based materials, aromatic compounds, and polymers, discussing their structures and superconducting properties, and propose new material platforms and experimental approaches.
result: The review summarizes progress in organic superconductors and outlines strategies such as new material construction, carrier doping, high-pressure application, and heterojunction formation.
conclusion: Organic systems offer promising routes toward high-temperature superconductivity, and targeted materials discovery and experimental methods may accelerate progress.

title: Selective Sparsity–enhanced Synchronization In Disordered Semiconductor Laser Networks
authors: Li-Li Yenathan Vignefan-Yi Linhui Caoying-Cheng Laiahttps://ror.org/03efmqc40school Of Electrical, Computer And Energy Engineering, Arizona State University, Tempe, AZ 85287bhttps://ror.org/03v76x132department Of Applied Physics, Yale University, New Haven, CT 06520chttps://ror.org/00zdnkx70institute Of Photonics Technologies, Department Of Electrical Engineering, National Tsing Hua University, Hsinchu 30013, Taiwandhttps://ror.org/03efmqc40department Of Physics, Arizona State University, Tempe, AZ 85287
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 41, October 2026.
SignificanceWhile biological networks efficiently use sparse connections, getting engineered systems like laser arrays to operate in perfect synchronization is intuitively expected to require resource-intensive coupling to overcome frequency differences. ...
tldr: The paper studies how selective sparsity can enhance synchronization in disordered networks of semiconductor lasers.
motivation: Biological networks achieve efficient synchronization with sparse connections, inspiring interest in whether engineered laser arrays can similarly exploit sparse coupling rather than resource-intensive all-to-all coupling.
method: The authors analyze synchronization dynamics in disordered semiconductor laser networks and examine the role of selective sparse coupling in overcoming frequency disorder.
result: Selective sparsity is found to improve synchronization performance in disordered laser networks, challenging the intuition that dense coupling is always required.
conclusion: Sparse, selectively designed coupling offers an efficient route to synchronizing semiconductor laser arrays and may inform network-based photonic engineering.

title: Percolation Dissipation Of The Α And ...
authors: Sheng-Hao Zeng, Bo-Yan Wang, Liang Gao, Qun Yang, Jun-Ying Jiang, Zi-Yi Ren, Jeppe C Dyre And Hai-Bin Yu
abstract: Dynamic processes in glasses are crucial for unraveling fundamentals of the glass transition and material properties. A recent theoretical framework proposes a ‘double-percolation’ scenario for the and -relaxation processes. While supported by simulations, no experimental validation has so far been presented. We here conduct a comprehensive analysis of the relaxation dissipation of more than 300 mechanical spectra of metallic glass samples. Our study yields two key findings, both aligning with the double-percolation theory: (i) The -relaxation has a damping factor of 0.6 ( 0.05), independent of material composition, probing frequency, and thermal history—a signature that is consistent with the percolation of immobile atomic clusters proposed to characterize the -relaxation. (ii) The -relaxation dissipation, though of variable magnitude and dependent on external factors, can be rationalized as caused by the percolation of mobile atomic entities driving configurational rearrangements; thus for the -relaxation we show that certain atomic motions are neither dissipative nor induce configurational changes. These results bridge theoretical predictions with experimental observations, suggesting a generally applicable picture of the atomic-scale mechanisms of relaxation dissipation in glass formers.
tldr: A large-scale experimental analysis of mechanical relaxation spectra in metallic glasses tests and supports a 'double-percolation' scenario for alpha- and beta-relaxation dissipation.
motivation: Dynamic relaxation processes in glasses are central to understanding the glass transition, but the recently proposed double-percolation theory has only been supported by simulations and lacked experimental validation.
method: The authors analyze more than 300 mechanical spectra of metallic glass samples, extracting damping factors and dissipation magnitudes for the alpha- and beta-relaxation processes and comparing them against percolation-theory predictions.
result: The beta-relaxation exhibits a composition-, frequency-, and thermal-history-independent damping factor of about 0.6, while alpha-relaxation dissipation is rationalized as arising from percolation of mobile atomic entities driving configurational rearrangements.
conclusion: The findings bridge theoretical predictions with experimental observation, supporting a general picture of atomic-scale relaxation dissipation in glass formers and indicating that certain atomic motions are neither dissipative nor configurationally relevant.

title: Nonflow Subtraction Beyond Two-particle Correlations
authors: Zaining Wang, Jiangyong Jia, Jinhui Chen, Shengli Huang, Chunjian Zhang And Zhengxi Yan
abstract: Establishing collective flow in small collision systems is a crucial and necessary condition for pinning down the minimum conditions for quark-gluon plasma formation. In two-particle correlations, nonflow has been subtracted with good control, pushing the reach of flow measurements down to very small event particle multiplicity . However, the multi-particle nature of collectivity has not been established in the same regime, because the residual nonflow surviving the subevent procedure in multi-particle cumulants has never been quantified. We develop a general nonflow subtraction framework for -particle cumulants, built around the approximate scaling of nonflow in the independent-source picture. Correlators containing serve as nonflow-dominated estimators, since the -integrated dipolar flow is expected to be small. title: The Higgs Boson, Naturalness, And The Universe

abstract: The Higgs boson—the only known fundamental scalar particle—may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.

conclusion: The Higgs field may have shaped the Universe from early times to the present, but the work lies in particle physics and cosmology and does not address the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Beyond Bulk Physics: Interfacial And Confinement Effects In Aqueous Microdroplets
authors: Anusuya Pal, Chiho Watanabe, Kazutoshi Masuda, Chen Chen And Miho Yanagisawa
abstract: Aqueous microdroplets provide a mesoscopic platform for investigating aqueous solutions under finite confinement. Despite their compositional diversity, including emulsions, vesicles, biomolecular condensates, synthetic cells, and living cells, these systems share a common physical setting defined by finite volume and a high surface-to-volume ratio, through which interfaces become dynamically coupled to the confined interior. At these length scales, neither molecular descriptions nor macroscopic continuum theories can fully describe confined aqueous systems, and concepts and measurement strategies developed for bulk solutions cannot always be applied directly. This review presents a physics-based framework for understanding how confinement and interfaces influence experimentally accessible physical observables, including mechanics, molecular transport, partitioning, electrostatic interactions, and phase behavior. Rather than organizing the literature by material systems, we focus on how to interpret these observables, summarize representative experimental approaches along with their physical assumptions and limitations, and discuss how finite confinement influences measurement interpretation and the applicability of bulk theoretical frameworks. By highlighting shared physical characteristics across diverse aqueous microdroplet systems, this review provides a conceptual bridge between traditional bulk studies and confined aqueous solutions. We conclude by discussing future challenges toward establishing a quantitative framework that consistently incorporates interfaces, finite confinement, and finite-size effects in synthetic and biological compartments.
tldr: This review presents a physics-based framework for understanding how interfaces and finite confinement affect physical observables in aqueous microdroplets.
motivation: Aqueous microdroplets across emulsions, vesicles, biomolecular condensates, synthetic cells, and living cells share finite-volume and high-surface-to-volume conditions that complicate the direct application of bulk theories.
method: The authors organize the literature by experimentally accessible observables—mechanics, molecular transport, partitioning, electrostatics, and phase behavior—rather than by material system, and they discuss measurement assumptions and limitations.
result: The review synthesizes representative experimental approaches and explains how finite confinement alters measurement interpretation and the applicability of bulk theoretical frameworks.
conclusion: It provides a conceptual bridge between bulk aqueous-solution studies and confined microdroplet systems, and identifies future challenges for a quantitative framework incorporating interfaces and finite-size effects.

title: Parallel Adaptive Reweighting Importance Sampling For Bayesian Astrophysics
authors: Miaoxin Liu And Alvin J K Chua
abstract: Efficient sampling from high-dimensional, multi-modal posteriors is a central challenge in Bayesian inference across the physical sciences. Gravitational-wave (GW) astronomy, where likelihood evaluations are computationally expensive and posteriors are complex, is one application motivating this work. Popular families of methods like Markov-chain Monte Carlo, Snested sampling, and importance sampling (IS) all rely on proposal distributions to guide exploration. Because prior knowledge of the target is often limited, practitioners can adopt adaptive proposals that iteratively refine themselves using information gained from previously drawn samples. Traditional adaptive strategies, however, struggle in high-dimensional multi-modal settings: complex, non-linear correlations are hard to capture, and hyperparameters typically require tedious, problem-specific tuning. To address these issues, we introduce parallel adaptive reweighting IS (PARIS; descriptively, ‘seed sampling’). PARIS models its proposal as a Gaussian mixture whose component centers are the existing samples and whose component weights match the current importance weights. New draws from the proposal therefore concentrate around high-weight regions, while candidate points in unexplored areas receive intentionally inflated weights. As the algorithm continuously reweights all samples up to the latest proposal, any initial over-weighting self-corrects once additional neighbor samples are collected. To enable rapid reweighting, we present an efficient update scheme and evaluate PARIS on illustrative toy problems and more realistic GW parameter estimation tasks. PARIS achieves accurate posterior reconstruction and evidence estimation with substantially fewer function evaluations than competing approaches, highlighting its promise for widespread use in astrophysical data analysis.
tldr: PARIS introduces a parallel adaptive reweighting importance sampling scheme using Gaussian-mixture proposals built from existing samples to efficiently sample high-dimensional, multi-modal Bayesian posteriors in gravitational-wave astrophysics.
motivation: Posterior sampling in high-dimensional, multi-modal settings with expensive likelihoods is hard for MCMC, nested sampling, and standard importance sampling, since adaptive proposals are difficult to tune and fail to capture complex correlations.
method: The proposal is modeled as a Gaussian mixture centered on existing samples with weights matching current importance weights; an efficient incremental reweighting update scheme lets all samples be reweighted against the latest proposal, with inflated weights in unexplored regions that self-correct as neighbors accumulate.
result: On toy problems and realistic gravitational-wave parameter estimation tasks, PARIS achieves accurate posterior reconstruction and evidence estimation with substantially fewer likelihood evaluations than competing samplers.
conclusion: PARIS offers a practical, largely tuning-free adaptive importance sampling approach with promise for widespread use in astrophysical data analysis and beyond.

Our analysis demonstrates that CISS does not function as a generic amplifier of magnetic sensitivity. Claimed enhancements are conditional on the relative alignment of the internal hyperfine and dipolar interaction axes, arising specifically under conditions of non-collinear internal interactions. Extension to a two-nucleus model confirms that these enhancements are sensitive to nuclear spin. CISS-induced effects observed in the single-nucleus model are substantially suppressed when a second collinear nucleus is introduced, with the exception of the hyperfine axis rotation sweep where non-collinear tensor misalignment drives a robust antisymmetric response. These findings indicate that the conditions for CISS-enhanced magnetoreception are more stringent than previously demonstrated, requiring highly ordered and rigid molecular geometries to sustain the effect.
